chapter: La Cigalle and settling in Paris
title: The French and Italian tours with Coleman, then La Cigalle
summary: Waters describes the French tour with Guy Lafitte reaching Casablanca, a six-week Italian tour, and leaving Coleman for the Cigalle with Jacques Butler.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We're probably getting a little bit ahead of our story. So you're in France in 1953 and Bill Coleman is organizing a new band. And you and Bill are the only Americans in the band, the rest were all French musicians?
Well, we went to Paris -
Yeah, when you went to Paris you're rehearsing in Paris -
Beofre us was another group -
Right, I know. But you're rehearsing in Paris and then you go on a French tour,
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
this would be '53.
Yeah, around '54 maybe, see -
It may even be that late -
Yeah, something, you know, something like that, see.
Uh huh.
Anyway, I wasn't working no place, see, till we get some tours - I worked with the band, see, I worked with the band around Germany and -
Switzerland -
And Switzerland before we went to Paris -
I know, right, right. You finished, you completed the tour, I understood that. You completed the tour, you arrive in Paris, you rehearse a new band. Then you go on a second tour around France.
Yes, because we even imported Guy Lafitte, you know probably Guy Lafitte -
Sure, Guy Lafitte, yeah -
We even imported Guy Lafitte from Paris and did quite a few dates with Guy Lafitte, you know what I mean?
Um hum.
So we didn't go right away. When Bill's guys left we got replacements, see. But when we went back, when we went on the tour -
The French tour -

Then we had to get Gormand [?] , we had to get the other piano player, we had another one, a guy that he didn't want to go on the tour yet. So we had Guy, Guy didn't go either because - so we had to take a trombone player and play some gigs, you know, like that. But we did this tour and went all the way to Casablanca and down there, in the Canaries [?] , you know. Everybody came back and we - I still stay with Bill, see, I'm still with Bill, see, because we wrestled with that tour together - long tour, see, about, at least a month. Then I rest around, fool around in Paris, fool around and catch the sights. And then we did another tour in Italy, that was six weeks. Then that tour, after that tour I leave and go to the Cigalle, I go to the Cigalle with Jacques Butler.
